title: Oval-Pan Tilapia Florentine
description: A soft spinach and Parmesan sauce surrounds thin tilapia fillets as they cook gently under cover in individual oval pans.
equipment: Two small oval cast iron pans with foil or fitted lids
Immersion blender and deep heatproof jug

ingredients.name: skinless tilapia fillet
ingredients.note: Weight after skin and pin bones are removed. Divide into two even portions about 1/2 inch thick. Fully thaw before cooking.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Choose unsalted plain meat-and-water broth without a vegetable blend.

steps.title: Wilt the spinach
steps.text: Cook {spinach} with {broth} in the covered HexClad over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes until tender.

steps.title: Blend the spinach milk
steps.text: Blend the spinach and cooking broth with {milk} until smooth and uniformly green.

steps.title: Make a pale roux
steps.text: Melt {butter} in the empty skillet over low heat. Whisk in {flour} for 1–2 minutes until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the Florentine sauce
steps.text: Gradually add the spinach milk to the roux, whisking over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Add the Parmesan
steps.text: Take off heat and stir in {parmesan} and {nutmeg}. Divide half the sauce between the two oval pans. Reserve the other half in the covered HexClad.

steps.title: Poach in the ovals
steps.text: Divide {fish} between the ovals and spoon some sauce over the top. Cover each pan and heat on low until tiny bubbles appear at the edge. Check from 3 minutes and then every minute. Pull each fillet at 135°F, usually after 4–8 minutes of gentle cooking.

steps.title: Rest under sauce
steps.text: Nestle the fish in the reserved warm Florentine sauce in the HexClad off heat. Spoon sauce over the top, cover and rest for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Check carryover and doneness
steps.text: After resting, check each thickest center for about 140°F. Open a natural seam with a fork. The center should be opaque and separate easily into flakes. If either cue is unclear or the center is below 140°F, finish covered in hot sauce in the HexClad over low heat to a measured 145°F, checking every minute.

steps.title: Heat the pan sauce
steps.text: While the fish stays covered in the HexClad, bring the sauce left in each oval to a bubbling simmer for 1 minute, stirring.

steps.title: Spoon into bowls
steps.text: Divide the hot oval-pan sauce between shallow bowls. Lay the tilapia over it and spoon the reserved green sauce over each fillet.

notes: Sauce yield: About 1 1/2 cups for two. Make ahead: Wilt and blend the spinach base a day ahead and chill it. Make the roux just before cooking. Refrigerate in shallow portions within 2 hours. Use refrigerated leftovers within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. Thin tilapia flakes easily and the spinach cream can weep after thawing. If already frozen, reheat one covered portion slowly and stir the sauce smooth. Fridge reheat: Warm a portion covered in its sauce over medium-low heat in the HexClad. Add a little water if it has thickened in storage. Check from 5 minutes and heat to 165°F at the coldest center. Freezer reheat: If frozen, thaw the covered portion in the refrigerator overnight, then follow the fridge method. For dairy-free sauce, use avocado oil, plain unsweetened oat milk and a little extra nutmeg in place of butter, milk and Parmesan. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 237 kcal, 34.2 g protein, 8.8 g total carbohydrate, 7.3 g fat, 0.6 g fiber, 200 mg sodium. Includes both the fish and its full share of sauce and any rice or potatoes listed. Sodium varies with the broth.
